reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: All five 4-point rows checked independently. A: with τ=t−2 s, the SI expressions are v=−1+2τ and s=5−τ+τ². Reversal occurs at t=2.5 s, s=4.75 m; s(3)=5 m and s(4)=7 m. Acceleration area gives Δv=4 m/s; signed velocity areas are −0.25 m and +2.25 m, giving displacement +2 m and distance 2.50 m. The predicted 7 m lies within [6.98,7.08] m. B: v=6−2t and s=6t−t² until stopping at 3 s and 9 m. Program continuation predicts v(5)=−4 m/s and s(5)=5 m, hence reverse motion. Continued rest instead requires s=9 m and v=a=0 after stopping. Both solutions are correct. The candidate repairs the original's mandatory shifted-time method, unsupported reference to resolution, and insufficiently explicit numerical request.

reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: Both 8-point rows checked. A: x/t=2.0 m/s and falling-distance/t²=5.00,5.00,4.8889 m/s² support approximately quadratic fall. Combined with linear horizontal motion and shared time, this supports an approximately parabolic trajectory. Superproportional growth alone, used in the original explanation, is insufficient. The candidate correctly acknowledges missing measurement-error bounds. B: reaction distances are 13.8889 m and 27.7778 m; stopping distances are 27.8889 m and 83.7778 m, with ratio approximately 3.00398. Doubling speed doubles reaction distance and quadruples the supplied braking distance. The stationary-obstacle interpretation makes this stopping-clearance judgment appropriate. Two supplied braking values do not establish a universal road or vehicle law.

reviews.scientificAndNumericalReview: Both languages and all 36 individual criteria, 1.1–6.6, checked. Correct SI laws are x=2t, y=1.25−5t², vy=−10t and ay=−10 m/s². At 0.20 s, x=0.40 m and y=1.05 m. Impact occurs at 0.500 s, with range 1.00 m and velocity components +2.00 and −5.00 m/s. The trajectory is y=1.25 m−(1.25 m⁻¹)x². Doubling horizontal speed preserves flight time and doubles range to 2.00 m. Graph descriptions and model reasoning are correct. Drag can affect vertical motion and couple it to overall motion; unequal arrival times or a universal arrival order are not required conclusions. The original rounding rules conflict: terminal rounding 1.25→1.3 differs by 4%, and 1.05→1.1 by approximately 4.76%. The candidate correctly accepts these two-significant-figure final results while requiring unrounded values for subsequent calculations.
